For a closed ticket the check runs at `end` but writes the tightened baseline into the working tree at the current HEAD, so a later change of the baseline (a line the person added) is overwritten and lines are dropped against a tree they were never judged on; Design SR1-2 (read equals write because the tree is clean) does not hold when the checked commit is not HEAD; no test covers a closed ticket with guards.

The tightened baseline is built from the baseline at the checked commit and written over the working-tree file without comparing the two, so a check at a commit other than the working tree's can re-add removed violations or drop newer lines, and AC-15 lets the check stay current over it.

The tightening write uses std::fs::write on root/<dir>/<baseline>, which follows a symlink, so a working-tree baseline that is a link makes the check write to any target, even outside the repository; no test covers it.

A ratchet guard that crashes with exit 1 (a Python traceback, an uncaught exception, a set -e script) and prints nothing on stdout counts as a list with no violations; every baseline line is fixed, the check writes an empty baseline, AC-15 keeps the check current, and the design decision 'a guard that cannot run never empties its baseline' is false.
A ratchet guard whose command fails with exit 1 and empty stdout passes and its baseline is rewritten empty, silently resetting the ratchet (same cause as XR1-3).

guards_write_ask loads the config with Config::parse_at, which also validates a pinned [check] cargo, while decide_write uses Config::parse; when the pin fails validation the guards rule is skipped and always_writable or the build permit allow a write into the guards folder, breaking AC-12.

The hook resolves the write target but compares it with the unresolved <root>/<dir>, so when dir or a parent part is a symlink, writes through the link and to the real folder both miss the guards rule and fall to the old write rules.

Proposal: a guard's command may read scripts or tool configs outside the guards folder (./scripts/coverage.sh, .eslintrc, clippy.toml, .rgignore) that an agent edits freely; warn when a command names no path under dir, or say in the skill and starter that guard scripts and their configs belong in dir, or list it in Not promised.
